paper.title: Leveraging priors on distribution functions for multi-arm bandits

settings.name_in_paper: K-arm bandit with sigma-sub-Gaussian rewards, Bayesian regret (nonparametric prior on reward distributions)
unmapped: the reward-vector distribution p* is itself drawn from a nonparametric prior (Dirichlet process prior on reward distributions)
settings.definition_quote: In this paper, we choose $\chi$ to the set of $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian random variables ... The “true reward-vector distribution” $p^\star$ is seen as a distribution over $\chi^{|\mathcal{A}|}$ that is itself randomly drawn from the family of distributions $\mathcal{P}$. We assume that, conditioned on $p^\star$, $(R_{t})_{t\in N}$ is an iid sequence ... we study the expected regret or Bayesian regret

conditions: DP prior DP(alpha, F_0) with base measure F_0 a sigma-sub-Gaussian distribution
expectation over the prior of the environment (prior assumed to be the DP prior used by the algorithm)
tuning: DP prior DP(alpha, F_0) with sigma-sub-Gaussian F_0

source.label: thm:Bayesian-regret-DPPS
source.quote: For the setting of $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian arm reward distributions, starting with a DP-prior, $\DP(\alpha, F_{0})$, with $F_{0}$ as a $\sigma$ sub-Gaussian distribution, the Bayesian regret of DPPS satisfies, \[\E\left[\mathrm{Regret}(T,\pi^{DPPS})\right] \le \sigma\sqrt{2{K}(\log{K})T}\,,\] where the expectation is taken over the randomness in the policy and the prior of the environment.

results.notes: Derived via Russo & Van Roy information-ratio analysis; proof is informal. Algorithm pseudocode lists horizon T as input but does not use it beyond the loop; bound holds for any T, so marked anytime. Polynomial compute (O(n) per arm per round, stick-breaking truncation).
